core_obligations: Reduce to X = Spec(A) affine using locality of the Noetherian property (proof lines 2324-2327).
Converse direction: the map from A to k' tensor_k A is faithfully flat, so Noetherianness descends (proof lines 2328-2330).
Forward direction: if A is Noetherian then so is k' tensor_k A because k'/k is a finitely generated field extension (proof lines 2331-2332).
proof_roadmap: Descent along the faithfully flat map (proof lines 2328-2330).
Base change of Noetherian algebras (proof lines 2331-2332).
difficulty_reason: For a scheme X over a field k and a finitely generated field extension k'/k, the lemma shows that X is locally Noetherian exactly when its base change is (statement lines 2314-2321). The proof reduces to the affine case using locality of the Noetherian property, arriving at the statement that A is Noetherian if and only if k' tensor_k A is; the forward direction is the standard behaviour of Noetherian rings under a field extension, and the converse is descent of Noetherianness along the faithfully flat map to the tensor product (proof lines 2323-2332). The claim is H2: a locality reduction plus the two directions of the tensor product statement, each a single cited input, with the finite generation hypothesis used precisely for the forward direction.
